s.d: ῥοιζηδόν adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow), with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): [[2-peter 3 10|2Pe.3:10.]]† (AS)

ῥομφαία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב ;] a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: [[revelation 1 16|Rev.1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21]]; metaphorically, [[luke 2 35|Luk.2:35.]]† (AS)
Ῥουβήν, ὁ indecl., (Heb. רְאוּבֵן), Reuben: [[revelation 7 5|Rev.7:5.]]† (AS)
Ῥoύθ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רוּת), Ruth: [[matthew 15 1|Mat.15:1-39.]]† (AS)
Ῥοῦφος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.), Rufus: [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]], [[romans 16 13|Rom.16:13]].† (AS)
Ῥοῦφος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.), Rufus: [[mark 15 21|Mrk.15:21]], [[romans 16 13|Rom.16:13]].† (AS)

ῥύμη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: [[isaiah 15 3|Isa.15:3]] (רְחֹב), [[proverbs 31 23|Pro.31:23]] א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1* ;] 1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers. 2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, [[matthew 6 2|Mat.6:2]], [[luke 14 21|Luk.14:21]] [[acts 9 11|Act.9:11 12:10]] (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).† (AS)

ῥύομαι [in LXX chiefly for נָצַל hi., also for גָּאַל, פָּלַט pi., etc. ;] to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 27 43|Mat.27:43]], [[2-peter 2 7|2Pe.2:7]]; id. before ἀπό, [[matthew 6 13|Mat.6:13]], [[luke 11 4|Luk.11:4]] (Rec., R, mg.), [[2-timothy 4 18|2Ti.4:18;]] before ἐκ, [[romans 7 24|Rom.7:24]], [[2-corinthians 1 10|2Co.1:10]], [[colossians 1 13|Col.1:13]], [[1-thessalonians 1 10|1Th.1:10]], [[2-timothy 3 11|2Ti.3:11]], [[2-peter 2 9|2Pe.2:9]]; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, [[romans 11 26|Rom.11:26.]] Passive: before ἀπό, [[romans 15 31|Rom.15:31]], [[2-thessalonians 3 2|2Th.3:2]]; before ἐκ, [[luke 1 74|Luk.1:74]], [[2-timothy 4 17|2Ti.4:17]].† (AS)
ῥυπαρία, -ας, ἡ (ῥυπαρός) filthiness: metaphorically, of moral defile­ment, [[james 1 21|Jas.1:21.]]† (AS)

ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν (ῥύπος), [in LXX: [[zechariah 3 4|Zec.3:4-5]], (3-4) (צוֹא)* ;] filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), [[james 2 2|Jas.2:2;]] metaphorically, of moral defilement, [[revelation 22 11|Rev.22:11.]]† (AS)
ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: [[isaiah 4 4|Isa.4:4]] (צוֹאָה), [[job 14 4|Job.14:4]] (טָמֵא), etc. ;] dirt, filth: [[1-peter 3 21|1Pe.3:21.]]† (AS)
ῥυπόω, -ῶ (ῥύπος), to make filthy: [[revelation 22 11|Rev.22:11]] Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).† (AS)
ῥύσις, -εως, ἡ (ῥέω), [in LXX chiefly for זוֹב ;] a flowing, issue: τ. αἵματος, [[mark 5 25|Mrk.5:25]], [[luke 8 43|Luk.8:43-44]].† (AS)
a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)
Roman, a Roman , (Polybius Historicus), etc.; adverb -κῶς, in Latin , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)
Ῥωμαϊστί adv., in Latin: [[john 19 20|Jhn.19:20.]]† (AS)

ῥώννυμι [in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 11:21 2Mac 11:28 2Mac 11:33 2Mac 11:1-38; 3Ma.6:1-41 * ;] to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): [[acts 15 29|Act.15:29 23:30]] Rec., R, mg.† (AS)

σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי), sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: [[matthew 27 46|Mat.27:46]], [[mark 15 34|Mrk.15:34]] ([[psalms 22 2|Psa.22:2]], Heb. עָזַב).† ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב), zaphthanei: [[matthew 27 46|Mat.27:46]] (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).† (AS)

σαβαώθ indecl., [in LXX for צָבָא, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; see DB, iii, 137 f.) ;] Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (see DB, l.with): [[romans 9 29|Rom.9:29]] (LXX), Ja 54.† (AS)

σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, [[exodus 16 30|Exo.16:30]], al.), a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaphorically, as in Mishna (Zorell, see word), [[hebrews 4 9|Heb.4:9.]]† (AS)

σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά [in LXX for שַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּתוֹן ;] 1. the seventh day of the week, the sabbath (a) the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: [[matthew 12 8|Mat.12:8]], [[mark 2 27|Mrk.2:27]], [[luke 6 5|Luk.6:5]], al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, [[exodus 20 8|Exo.20:8]], al., usually τῶν σ., see infr.), [[luke 13 16|Luk.13:16 14:5]]; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, [[acts 1 12|Act.1:12]] (cf. [[matthew 24 29|Mat.24:29]]); dative, of time (τῷ) σ., [[luke 6 9|Luk.6:9 14:1]]; ἐν (τῷ) σ., [[matthew 12 2|Mat.12:2]], [[luke 6 7|Luk.6:7]], [[john 5 16|Jhn.5:16]], al.; accusative, of duration, τὸ σ., [[luke 23 56|Luk.23:56;]] κατὰ πᾶν σ., [[acts 13 27|Act.13:27 15:21 18:4]]; pl., σ. τρία, [[acts 17 2|Act.17:2]] R, txt. (but see infr.); (b) as most frequently in LXX (see Swete, Mk., 17; Thackeray, Gr., 35) the pl. form, τὰ σ. (see supr. on the Aram. form. There is also an analogy in the names of other festivals, τ. ἐγκαίνια, ἄζυμα, etc.): [[matthew 28 1|Mat.28:1]], [[colossians 2 16|Col.2:16]]; ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν σ. ([[exodus 20 8|Exo.20:8]], al.), [[luke 4 16|Luk.4:16]], [[acts 13 14|Act.13:14 16:13]]; dative pl. (in LXX -τοις, but 1Ma.2:38 as in NT) by metaplasmus (El., § 9, 3), σάββασι, [[matthew 12 1|Mat.12:1, 5 12:10-12]] [[mark 1 21|Mrk.1:21 2:23 3:2, 4]], [[luke 4 31|Luk.4:31 6:2]]. 2. seven days, a week; (a) the sing. form: πρώτη σαββάτσυ, [[mark 16 9|Mrk.16:9;]] δὶς τοῦ σ. (Bl., § 35, 4; 36, 13), [[luke 18 12|Luk.18:12;]] κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου, [[1-corinthians 16 2|1Co.16:2;]] pl., σ. τρία, [[acts 17 2|Act.17:2]] R, mg. (but see supr.); (b) the pl. form: ἡ μία τῶν σ. (where the genitive = μετὰ τά; Soph., Lex., 43a), [[matthew 28 1|Mat.28:1]], [[mark 16 2|Mrk.16:2]], [[luke 24 1|Luk.24:1]], [[john 20 1|Jhn.20:1, 19]], [[acts 20 7|Act.20:7]] (AS)
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם ;] a drag-net, seine: [[matthew 13 47|Mat.13:47.]]† SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), δίκτυον (AS)
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος) Sadoc, Zadok: [[matthew 1 14|Mat.1:14.]]† (AS)

σαίνω 1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn. 2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., [[1-thessalonians 3 3|1Th.3:3]] (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).† (AS)

σάκκος also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ (cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX), 1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: [[revelation 6 12|Rev.6:12.]] 2. Anything made of sackcloth; (a) a sack ([[genesis 42 25|Gen.42:25]], al.); (b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: [[matthew 11 21|Mat.11:21]], [[luke 10 13|Luk.10:13]], [[revelation 11 3|Rev.11:3]].† (AS)
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח), Sala, Shalah: [[luke 3 32|Luk.3:32]] (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), [[luke 3 35|Luk.3:35.]]† (AS)
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח), Sala, Shalah: [[luke 3 32|Luk.3:32]] (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), [[luke 3 35|Luk.3:35.]]† (AS)
Σαλαθιήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל), Salathiel: [[matthew 1 12|Mat.1:12]], [[luke 3 27|Luk.3:27]].† (AS)
Σαλαθιήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל), Salathiel: [[matthew 1 12|Mat.1:12]], [[luke 3 27|Luk.3:27]].† (AS)
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνσς, ἡ Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: [[acts 13 5|Act.13:5.]]† (AS)
Σαλείμ, τό indecl., Salim: [[john 3 23|Jhn.3:23]] (see Westc., in l; DB, iii, 354).† (AS)

σαλεύω (σάλος), [in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc. ;] prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, [[matthew 11 7|Mat.11:7]], [[luke 7 24|Luk.7:24]]; a house, [[luke 6 48|Luk.6:48]], [[acts 4 31|Act.4:31 16:26]]; the earth, [[hebrews 12 26|Heb.12:26;]] the heavenly bodies, [[matthew 24 29|Mat.24:29]], [[mark 13 25|Mrk.13:25]], [[luke 21 26|Luk.21:26]]; of a vessel shaken in filling, [[luke 6 38|Luk.6:38.]] Metaphorical, (a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., [[hebrews 12 27|Heb.12:27;]] (b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: [[acts 2 25|Act.2:25]] (LXX); (with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, [[2-thessalonians 2 2|2Th.2:2;]] (d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, [[acts 17 13|Act.17:13.]]† (AS)
Σαλήμ, ἡ (Heb. שָׁלֵם [[genesis 14 18|Gen.14:18]]), Salem: [[hebrews 7 1|Heb.7:1-2]] (LXX).† (AS)
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן), Salmon: [[matthew 1 4|Mat.1:4-5]], [[luke 3 32|Luk.3:32]] (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).† (AS)
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ Salmone, a promontory of Crete: [[acts 27 7|Act.27:7.]]† (AS)
σάλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;] in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: [[luke 21 25|Luk.21:25.]]† (AS)

σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;] a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: [[1-corinthians 14 8|1Co.14:8]], [[hebrews 12 19|Heb.12:19]], [[revelation 1 10|Rev.1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14]] By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, [[matthew 24 31|Mat.24:31;]] ἐν σ. θεοῦ, [[1-thessalonians 4 16|1Th.4:16;]] ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., [[1-corinthians 15 52|1Co.15:52.]]† (AS)

σαλπίζω [in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;] to sound a trumpet: [[revelation 8 6|Rev.8:6]] ff. [[revelation 9 1|Rev.9:1, 13 10:7 11:15]]; metaphorically, [[matthew 6 2|Mat.6:2.]] Impers., the trumpet sounds: [[1-corinthians 15 52|1Co.15:52.]]† (AS)
σαλπιστής (so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ, a trumpeter: [[revelation 18 22|Rev.18:22.]]† (AS)
Σαλώμη, -ης, ἡ (Heb. שָׁלוֹם), Salome: [[mark 15 40|Mrk.15:40 16:1]].† (AS)

Σαμαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ (Heb. שֹׁמְרוֹן; Aram. שָׁמְרַיִן), Samaria; (a) the city: [[acts 8 5|Act.8:5]] (and perhaps also [[acts 8 9|Act.8:9, 14]]); (b) the region: [[luke 17 11|Luk.17:11]], [[john 4 4|Jhn.4:4-5]], 7, [[acts 1 8|Act.1:8 8:1]] (and perhaps also [[acts 8 9|Act.8:9, 14]]) [[acts 9 31|Act.9:31 15:3]].† (AS)

Σαμαρείτης (-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό, a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): [[matthew 10 5|Mat.10:5]], [[luke 9 52|Luk.9:52 10:33 17:16]], [[john 4 9|Jhn.4:9, 39-40]], [[acts 8 25|Act.8:25]]; as an opprobrious epithet, [[john 8 48|Jhn.8:48.]]† (AS)
Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, see supr.), -ιδος, ἡ 1. in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria. 2. a Samaritan woman: [[john 4 9|Jhn.4:9.]]† (AS)
Σαμοθρᾴκη (-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: [[acts 16 11|Act.16:11.]]† (AS)
Σάμος, -ου, ἡ Samos, an island in the Ægean: [[acts 20 15|Act.20:15.]]† (AS)
Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל), Samuel ([[1-kings 1 20|1Ki.1:20]], al.): [[acts 3 24|Act.3:24 13:20]], [[hebrews 11 32|Heb.11:32]].† (AS)
Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן), Samson ([[judges 13 1|Jdg.13:1-25]] ff.): [[hebrews 11 32|Heb.11:32]].† (AS)

σανδάλιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: [[joshua 9 5|Jos.9:5]], [[isaiah 20 2|Isa.20:2]] (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, which see), Jdth.10:4 16:9 * ;] a sandal: [[mark 6 9|Mrk.6:9]], [[acts 12 8|Act.12:8]].† (AS)
σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX: [[song-of-solomon 8 9|Sng.8:9]], [[ezekiel 27 5|Eze.27:5]] (לוּחַ) * ;] a board, plank: [[acts 27 44|Act.27:44]] (AS)

Σαούλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל) Saul; (a) the King of Israel: [[acts 13 21|Act.13:21;]] (b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): [[acts 9 4|Act.9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14]].† (AS)

Σαούλ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Σάουλος; Heb. שָׁאוּל) Saul; (a) the King of Israel: [[acts 13 21|Act.13:21;]] (b) the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): [[acts 9 4|Act.9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14]].† (AS)

σαπρός, -ά -όν [in Sm.: [[leviticus 27 14|Lev.27:14, 33]] * ;] rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός), [[matthew 7 17|Mat.7:17-18 12:33]] [[luke 6 43|Luk.6:43]]; of fish, [[matthew 13 48|Mat.13:48.]] Metaphorical, in moral sense: λόγος σ., [[ephesians 4 29|Eph.4:29.]] "In Hellenistic . . . it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.† (AS)
Σαπφείρα, -ης (see B1., § 3, 4), ἡ (Aram. שַׁפִּירָא) Sapphia: [[acts 5 1|Act.5:1.]]† (AS)
σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for סַפִּיר ;] sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): [[revelation 21 19|Rev.21:19.]]† (AS)
σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ 1. a plaited rope (Æsch.). 2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: [[2-corinthians 11 33|2Co.11:33.]]† (AS)
Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11 3:1, 4]] (AS)
σάρδινος, -ου, ὁ = σάρδιον (which see), [[revelation 4 3|Rev.4:3]], Rec.† (AS)
σάρδιον, -ον, τ [in LXX for אֹדֶם, [[exodus 28 17|Exo.28:17]], al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;] the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): [[revelation 4 3|Rev.4:3 21:20]].† (AS)
σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ (σάρδιον, ὄνυξ), sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: [[revelation 21 20|Rev.21:20.]]† (AS)
Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת), Sarepta, a city of Sidon: [[luke 4 26|Luk.4:26.]]† (AS)

σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (σάρξ) (seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7) = Lat. carnalis, i.e. (a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: [[romans 15 27|Rom.15:27]], [[1-corinthians 9 11|1Co.9:11]]; (b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): [[1-corinthians 3 3|1Co.3:3]], [[2-corinthians 1 12|2Co.1:12 10:4]], [[1-peter 2 11|1Pe.2:11]].† SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ LXXi, LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on [[romans 7 14|Rom.7:14]] (AS)

σάρκινος, -η, -ον (σάρξ), [in LXX: [[2-chronicles 32 8|2Ch.32:8]], [[ezekiel 11 19|Eze.11:19 36:26]] (בָּשָׂר), [[esther 4 17|Est.4:17]], [[proverbs 24 23|Pro.24:23]] ([[proverbs 29 27|Pro.29:27]]) * ;] = Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): [[romans 7 14|Rom.7:14]], [[1-corinthians 3 1|1Co.3:1]], [[2-corinthians 3 3|2Co.3:3]], [[hebrews 7 16|Heb.7:16]]. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except [[2-corinthians 3 3|2Co.3:3]], but the evidence is decisive against it.)† SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v (AS)

σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;] flesh; 1. as in cl. generally, (a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: [[1-corinthians 15 39|1Co.15:39]], [[2-corinthians 12 7|2Co.12:7]], [[galatians 6 13|Gal.6:13]], al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, [[1-corinthians 5 50|1Co.5:50;]] σ. καὶ ὀστέα, [[luke 24 39|Luk.24:39;]] pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), [[revelation 17 16|Rev.17:16 19:18]]; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. with (cf. κατεσθίειν, [[2-kings 9 36|4Ki.9:36]], al., and βιβρώσκειν, frequently in l.); metaphorically, [[james 5 3|Jas.5:3;]] mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, [[john 6 52|Jhn.6:52-56;]] (b) Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: [[acts 2 26|Act.2:26]] (LXX), 31, [[2-corinthians 12 7|2Co.12:7]], [[galatians 4 14|Gal.4:14]], [[ephesians 5 29|Eph.5:29]]; μία σ., [[mark 10 8|Mrk.10:8;]] εἰς σ. μίαν ([[genesis 2 24|Gen.2:24]]), [[matthew 19 5|Mat.19:5]], [[mark 10 8|Mrk.10:8]], [[1-corinthians 6 16|1Co.6:16]], [[ephesians 5 31|Eph.5:31]]; hence, of the material as opposite to the immaterial part of man (cf. Lft., Notes, 88): opposite to πνεῦμα, [[1-corinthians 5 5|1Co.5:5]], [[2-corinthians 7 1|2Co.7:1]], [[colossians 2 5|Col.2:5]], [[1-peter 3 18|1Pe.3:18, 4:6]]; to ψύχη, [[acts 2 31|Act.2:31]], Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., [[romans 7 5|Rom.7:5]], [[galatians 2 20|Gal.2:20]], [[philippians 1 22|Php.1:22, 24]] [[1-peter 4 2|1Pe.4:2]]; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, [[hebrews 5 7|Heb.5:7;]] of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., [[galatians 6 12|Gal.6:12, 13]] [[philippians 3 3|Php.3:3]], 4. 2. As in Heb. idiom, (a) of a living creature: πᾶσα σ. (Heb. כָּל־בָּשָׂר; cf. Bl., §47, 9), [[matthew 24 22|Mat.24:22]], [[mark 13 20|Mrk.13:20]], [[1-peter 1 24|1Pe.1:24]]; esp. of man and his mortality (Psa.55 (56):5, Sir.28:5, al.), [[john 1 14|Jhn.1:14]]; πᾶσα σ. (see supr.), [[luke 3 6|Luk.3:6]], [[john 17 2|Jhn.17:2]], [[acts 2 17|Act.2:17]], ἐν σ., 1Jo.4:2, [[1-timothy 3 16|1Ti.3:16]]; (b) of natural origin and relationship ([[genesis 2 24|Gen.2:24]], [[isaiah 58 7|Isa.58:7]], al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., [[romans 9 8|Rom.9:8;]] κατὰ σάρκα, ib. 3, 5, [[1-corinthians 10 18|1Co.10:18]], [[galatians 4 23|Gal.4:23, 29]]; ἡ σ. μου, [[romans 11 14|Rom.11:14]] (cf. [[judges 9 2|Jdg.9:2]], [[2-samuel 5 1|2Ki.5:1]], al.). 3. Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.), (a) without any ethical disparagement: [[romans 7 18|Rom.7:18 13:14]]; opposite to πνεῦμα, [[matthew 26 41|Mat.26:41]], [[mark 14 38|Mrk.14:38]]; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., [[john 1 13|Jhn.1:13;]] ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., [[1-john 2 16|1Jn.2:16;]] pl., [[2-peter 2 18|2Pe.2:18;]] παθεῖν σαρκί, [[1-peter 4 1|1Pe.4:1;]] (b) in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opposite to νοῦς, [[romans 7 25|Rom.7:25;]] to πνεῦμα, [[romans 8 4|Rom.8:4-9, 12, 13]], [[galatians 5 16|Gal.5:16, 17 19 6:8]] (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844ff.). (AS)
Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג), Serug: [[luke 3 35|Luk.3:35.]]† (AS)
σαρόω, -ῶ late form of σαίρω, to sweep: with accusative, [[luke 15 8|Luk.15:8;]] pass., [[matthew 12 44|Mat.12:44]], [[luke 11 25|Luk.11:25]].† (AS)
Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, [[genesis 17 15|Gen.17:15]]), Sarah: [[romans 4 19|Rom.4:19 9:9]], [[hebrews 11 11|Heb.11:11]], [[1-peter 3 6|1Pe.3:6]].† (AS)
Σάρων, -ωνος (accusative -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן), the plain of Sharon: [[acts 9 35|Act.9:35.]]† (AS)
Satan , i. e. an adversary, enemy : name for the Devil , (New Testament) Hebr. word. (ML)

Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ (so also Sir 21:30, but in [[1-kings 11 14|3Ki.11:14]], σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό, Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. with): [[matthew 4 10|Mat.4:10 12:26]], [[mark 1 13|Mrk.1:13 3:23, 26 4:15]] [[luke 10 18|Luk.10:18 11:18 13:16 22:3, 31]], [[john 13 27|Jhn.13:27]], [[acts 5 3|Act.5:3 26:18]], [[romans 16 20|Rom.16:20]], [[1-corinthians 5 5|1Co.5:5 7:5]], [[2-corinthians 2 11|2Co.2:11 11:14]], [[1-thessalonians 2 18|1Th.2:18]], [[2-thessalonians 2 9|2Th.2:9]], [[1-timothy 1 20|1Ti.1:20 5:15]], [[revelation 2 9|Rev.2:9, 13 2:24 3:9 12:9 20:2, 7]]; addressed in person of Peter, [[matthew 16 23|Mat.16:23]] [[mark 8 33|Mrk.8:33]]; ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, [[2-corinthians 12 7|2Co.12:7.]]† (AS)
σάτον, -ου, τό (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: [[haggai 2 17|Hag.2:17]] (16)* ;] a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): [[matthew 13 33|Mat.13:33]], [[luke 13 21|Luk.13:21]].† (AS)
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see), Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: [[acts 7 58|Act.7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9]].† (AS)
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see), Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: [[acts 7 58|Act.7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9]].† (AS)

σβέννυμι [in LXX chiefly for כָּבָה ;] of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, [[matthew 12 20|Mat.12:20]], [[ephesians 6 16|Eph.6:16]], [[hebrews 11 34|Heb.11:34]]; pass., [[matthew 25 8|Mat.25:8]], [[mark 9 48|Mrk.9:48]], [44, 46]. Metaphorical (cf. [[song-of-solomon 8 7|Sng.8:7]], 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, [[1-thessalonians 5 19|1Th.5:19.]]† ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, [[1-thessalonians 5 19|1Th.5:19]] T (see WH, Notes, 148).† (AS)

αὐτός, -ή, -ό, determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399). 1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, [[luke 5 37|Luk.5:37;]] αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, [[john 2 25|Jhn.2:25;]] αὐ.ὑμεῖς, [[john 3 28|Jhn.3:28;]] καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, [[romans 15 14|Rom.15:14;]] αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, [[john 2 24|Jhn.2:24;]] αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, [[mark 2 25|Mrk.2:25;]] ὑμεῖς αὐ., [[mark 6 31|Mrk.6:31;]] esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, [[matthew 3 4|Mat.3:4]], [[mark 6 17|Mrk.6:17]], [[john 16 27|Jhn.16:27]], [[1-thessalonians 3 11|1Th.3:11]], al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]] (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word); (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), [[matthew 1 21|Mat.1:21, 12:50]], [[luke 6 35|Luk.6:35]], al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), [[matthew 8 24|Mat.8:24]], [[mark 4 38|Mrk.4:38]], al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), [[matthew 14 2|Mat.14:2]], [[mark 14 15|Mrk.14:15, 44]], [[luke 1 22|Luk.1:22, 2:28]], al. 2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, [[matthew 7 9|Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44]], al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., [[matthew 9 18|Mat.9:18]], [[mark 13 1|Mrk.13:1]], al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), [[mark 7 25|Mrk.7:25]], [[revelation 3 8|Rev.3:8, 7:2]], al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, [[matthew 4 23|Mat.4:23]], [[acts 8 5|Act.8:5]], [[2-corinthians 2 13|2Co.2:13]], al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, [[romans 11 11|Rom.11:11]], [[1-thessalonians 2 19|1Th.2:19]], [[titus 3 5|Tit.3:5]], [[hebrews 2 4|Heb.2:4]]. 3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: [[hebrews 1 12|Heb.1:12, 13:8]]; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, [[matthew 5 46|Mat.5:46, 47]], al.; φρονεῖν, [[romans 12 16|Rom.12:16, 15:5]], [[philippians 2 2|Php.2:2]], al.; τὰ αὐ., [[acts 15 27|Act.15:27]], [[romans 2 1|Rom.2:1]], al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), [[acts 14 1|Act.14:1]], [[luke 6 23|Luk.6:23]], al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), [[matthew 22 34|Mat.22:34]], [[acts 1 15|Act.1:15]], al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., [[1-corinthians 11 5|1Co.11:5, 12:11]]; with dative (cl.), [[1-corinthians 11 5|1Co.11:5;]] with a noun, λόγος, [[mark 14 39|Mrk.14:39;]] μέτρος, [[philippians 1 30|Php.1:30;]] πνεῦμα, [[1-corinthians 12 4|1Co.12:4.]] (AS)

σεαυτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ (in NT not contracted, σαυτοῦ, as in Att..), reflex. prop. of 2nd of person(s) sing., used only in genitive, dative and accusative (of, to) thyself: [[matthew 4 6|Mat.4:6]], [[john 8 13|Jhn.8:13]], [[1-timothy 4 16|1Ti.4:16]], al. (In Hellenistic, the pl. is ἑαυτῶν (which see), not ὑμῶν αὐτῶν as in Attic, see Bl., § 13, 1.) † (AS)
σεβάζομαι (σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: [[hosea 10 5|Hos.10:5]] * ;] 1. to fear (Hom). 2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: [[romans 1 25|Rom.1:25]] (AS)
σέβασμα, -τος, τό (σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;] an object of worship: [[acts 17 23|Act.17:23]], [[2-thessalonians 2 4|2Th.2:4]].† (AS)

σεβαστός, -ή, -όν (σεβάζομαι) 1. reverend, august. 2. In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name; (a) ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: [[acts 25 21|Act.25:21, 25]]; (b) Augustan: σπείρα σ., [[acts 27 1|Act.27:1]] (See further, Deiss., BS, 218.) † (AS)

σέβω [in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, [[joshua 4 24|Jos.4:24]], al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. 4Ma.5:24 ;] to worship: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 15 9|Mat.15:9]], [[mark 7 7|Mrk.7:7]], [[acts 18 13|Act.18:13 19:27]]; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, [[acts 16 14|Act.16:14 18:7]]; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, [[acts 13 43|Act.13:43, 50 17:4, 17]] (cf. προσήλυτος).† (AS)

σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: [[judges 16 13|Jdg.16:13-14, 19]] (מַחְלָפָה), [[proverbs 5 22|Pro.5:22]] (חֶבֶל) * ;] 1. (a) a cord; (b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.with): σειραὶ ζόφου, [[2-peter 2 4|2Pe.2:4]], Rec., R, mg. (see: σειρός). 2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. with).† (AS)

σεισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ ;] a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: [[matthew 8 24|Mat.8:24;]] esp. an earthquake: [[matthew 24 7|Mat.24:7 27:54 28:2]], [[mark 13 8|Mrk.13:8]], [[luke 21 11|Luk.21:11]], [[acts 16 26|Act.16:26]], [[revelation 6 12|Rev.6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18]].† (AS)

σείω [in LXX chiefly for רָעַשׁ ;] to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, [[hebrews 12 26|Heb.12:26]] (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, [[matthew 27 51|Mat.27:51]] (LXX); συκῆ, [[revelation 6 13|Rev.6:13.]] Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: [[matthew 21 10|Mat.21:10 28:4]] (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).† (AS)
Σέκουνδος (Rec. Σεκοῦνδος), -ου, ὁ (Lat.), Secundus: [[acts 20 4|Act.20:4.]]† (AS)
Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια), Seleucia, a city of Syria: [[acts 13 4|Act.13:4.]]† (AS)

σελήνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ ([[genesis 37 9|Gen.37:9]], al.), also for לְבָנָה; ([[song-of-solomon 6 9|Sng.6:9]](10), ?[[isaiah 24 23|Isa.24:23 30:26]]) ;] the moon: [[matthew 24 29|Mat.24:29]], [[mark 13 24|Mrk.13:24]], [[luke 21 25|Luk.21:25]], [[acts 2 20|Act.2:20]]" (LXX), [[1-corinthians 15 41|1Co.15:41]], [[revelation 6 12|Rev.6:12 8:12 12:1 21:23]].† (AS)

σεληνιάζω (σελήνη), act, in Manetho (Caren., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι, to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): [[matthew 4 24|Mat.4:24 17:15]].† (AS)
Σεμεείν (Rec. Σεμεΐ), ὁ, indecl., Semein: [[luke 3 26|Luk.3:26.]]† (AS)
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;] fine wheaten flour: [[revelation 18 13|Rev.18:13.]]† (AS)

σεμνός, -ή, -όν (σέβομαι), [in LXX: [[proverbs 6 8|Pro.6:8 8:6 15:26]], 2Ma.6:11 2Mac 6:28 2Mac 8:15, 4Ma.5:36 4Mac 7:15 4Mac 17:5 * ;] 1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings. 2. grave, serious; of persons: [[1-timothy 3 8|1Ti.3:8 3:11]], [[titus 2 2|Tit.2:2]]; of things: [[philippians 4 8|Php.4:8]] (see Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).† (AS)
σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;] gravity: [[1-timothy 2 2|1Ti.2:2 3:4]] (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), [[titus 2 7|Tit.2:7.]]† (AS)
Σέργιος, -ου, ὁ Sergius, surnamed Paulus: [[acts 13 7|Act.13:7.]]† (AS)
Σήθ, ὁ (Heb. שֵׁת), indecl., Seth ([[genesis 4 25|Gen.4:25]]): [[luke 3 38|Luk.3:38]].† (AS)
Σήμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֵׁם), Shem: [[luke 3 36|Luk.3:36.]]† (AS)

σημαίνω (σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע, etc. ;] to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), [[acts 25 27|Act.25:27]], [[revelation 1 1|Rev.1:1]] (cf. MM, xxii); with accusative and inf., [[acts 11 28|Act.11:28;]] before quæst. indir., [[john 12 33|Jhn.12:33 18:32 21:19]].† (AS)

σημεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for אוֹת ;] a sign, mark, token; (a) of that which distinguishes a person or thing from others: [[matthew 26 48|Mat.26:48]] [[luke 2 12|Luk.2:12]], [[2-thessalonians 3 17|2Th.3:17]] (cf. Deiss., LAE, 153.2); before genitive epexeg., [[romans 4 11|Rom.4:11;]] with genitive obj., [[matthew 24 8|Mat.24:8, 30]], [[2-corinthians 12 12|2Co.12:12]]; with genitive subj., [[matthew 16 3|Mat.16:3;]] (b) a sign of warning or admonition: [[matthew 12 39|Mat.12:39 16:4]], [[luke 2 34|Luk.2:34 11:29-30]], [[1-corinthians 14 22|1Co.14:22]]; (with) a sign portending future events (Soph., Plat. al.): [[mark 13 4|Mrk.13:4]], [[luke 21 7|Luk.21:7, 11 21:25]], [[acts 2 19|Act.2:19]], [[revelation 12 1|Rev.12:1, 3 15:1]]; (d) of miracles and wonders (MM, xxii), regarded as signs of a divine authority: [[matthew 12 38|Mat.12:38-39 16:1, 4]] [[mark 8 11|Mrk.8:11-12]] [[luke 11 16|Luk.11:16, 29 23:8]], [[john 2 11|Jhn.2:11, 18 2:23 4:54 6:30 10:41 12:18]], [[acts 4 16|Act.4:16, 22]]; pl., [[mark 16 17|Mrk.16:17, 20]], [[john 2 11|Jhn.2:11, 23 3:2 6:2, 14 6:26 7:31 9:16 11:47 12:37 20:30]], [[acts 8 6|Act.8:6]], [[1-corinthians 1 22|1Co.1:22]] (Lft., Notes, 162); the same ascribed to false teachers and demons: [[matthew 24 24|Mat.24:24]], [[mark 13 22|Mrk.13:22]], [[2-thessalonians 2 9|2Th.2:9]], [[revelation 13 13|Rev.13:13-14 16:14 19:20]]; σ. καὶ τέρατα (τ. καὶ σ.; cf. Tr., Syn., § xci), [[matthew 24 24|Mat.24:24]], [[mark 13 22|Mrk.13:22]], [[john 4 48|Jhn.4:48]], [[acts 2 19|Act.2:19, 43 4:30 5:12 6:8 7:36 14:3 15:12]], [[romans 15 19|Rom.15:19]], [[2-thessalonians 2 9|2Th.2:9]]; id. before καὶ δυνάμεις, [[2-corinthians 12 12|2Co.12:12]], [[hebrews 2 4|Heb.2:4]]; σ. καὶ δυνάμεις, [[acts 8 13|Act.8:13;]] δ. καὶ τ. καὶ σ., [[acts 2 22|Act.2:22;]] σ. διδόναι, [[matthew 24 24|Mat.24:24]], [[mark 13 22|Mrk.13:22]].† (AS)
σημειόω, -ῶ (σημεῖον), [in LXX: [[psalms 4 6|Psa.4:6]] (נָשָׂא)* ;] to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: [[2-thessalonians 3 14|2Th.3:14]] (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).† (AS)

σήμερον (Att.. τήμερον), adv., [in LXX for יוֹם ;] to-day: [[matthew 6 11|Mat.6:11]], [[luke 4 21|Luk.4:21]], [[acts 4 9|Act.4:9]], al.; opposite to αὔριον, [[matthew 6 30|Mat.6:30]], [[luke 12 28|Luk.12:28]], [[james 4 13|Jas.4:13]]; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, [[hebrews 13 8|Heb.13:8;]] ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, [[acts 20 20|Act.20:20;]] ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, [[romans 11 8|Rom.11:8]], [[2-corinthians 3 14|2Co.3:14]]; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), [[matthew 11 23|Mat.11:23 27:8]]; as subst., τὸ σ., [[hebrews 3 13|Heb.3:13;]] id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμὶραν, σ., [[hebrews 4 7|Heb.4:7]] R, mg., (see Westc., in l) (AS)

σήπω [in LXX; [[psalms 38 5|Psa.38:5]] (מָקַק ni.), [[job 33 21|Job.33:21]] (כָּלָה) [[job 40 7|Job.40:7]], Sir.14:19, al. ;] to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (see M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, [[james 5 2|Jas.5:2.]]† (AS)

σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν (οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk), silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: [[revelation 18 12|Rev.18:12]] (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).† (AS)

σής σητός (late genitive for cl. σεός), ὁ, [in LXX: [[job 4 19|Job.4:19]], [[isaiah 50 9|Isa.50:9]] (עָשׁ), [[isaiah 51 8|Isa.51:8]] (סָס), al. ;] a moth, clothes moth: [[matthew 6 19|Mat.6:19-20]], [[luke 12 33|Luk.12:33]].† (AS)
σητό-βρωτος, -ον (οής, βιβρώσκω), [in LXX: [[job 13 28|Job.13:28]] (אָכַל עָשׁ) * ;] moth-eaten: [[james 5 2|Jas.5:2.]]† (AS)
σθενόω, -ῶ (σθένος, strength), to strengthen: with accusative, [[1-peter 5 10|1Pe.5:10]] (Hesych.).† (AS)
